document_title: One Line Out. Alaska's One Name on the AI Power Pledge
post_copy:
Cordova sits on Prince William Sound, off the state highway system, with no transmission line to another community.

Read on July 26, it is the only Alaska name on the White House pledge that AI load pays for its own power. Gov. Mike Dunleavy signed the governors addendum on July 23. It is non binding.

A binding version got close. SB 250 would have required commission approved contracts so data center costs stayed with the operator. It passed the Alaska Senate on May 16 and died in House Community and Regional Affairs.

4,700 acres at JBER, Eielson and Clear sit offered for data centers. Cordova's own runs on 150 kilowatts of hydro.

No Railbelt utility appears on the list. Inside, all 281 names and every megawatt on one axis.

So which should the next Alaska data center answer to, the pledge the governor signed or the bill the House let die?

#AlaskaEnergy #Railbelt #DataCenterPolicy

slides.headline: One Alaska utility signed. Its wires reach no one else.
281 names on the pledge. One of them is in Alaska.

slides.kicker: What signing asks of a company
slides.headline: Five commitments. Nobody has to keep them.
slides.body: USA TODAY and POWER both call the pledge non binding. Twenty three governors signed an addendum promising to implement its principles to the greatest extent possible.
labels: 01 BUILD, BRING OR BUY NEW POWER SUPPLY
02 PAY FOR NEW POWER DELIVERY INFRASTRUCTURE
03 PAY WHETHER THEY USE THE POWER OR NOT
04 INVEST IN LOCAL JOBS AND WORKFORCE
05 CONTRIBUTE TO GRID AND COMMUNITY RESILIENCE

slides.headline: 1,566 customers. 18 megawatts. No line out.
slides.body: Cordova Electric Cooperative runs one diesel plant and two hydroelectric plants. The town is off the state highway system and the cooperative is not connected by transmission line to any other community.
labels: CORDOVA DATA CENTER, 150 kW, ON HYDRO
"the American people should not be footing the bill for the benefit of private companies"
THE PLEDGE, AS QUOTED BY THE RGA

slides.headline: Every megawatt in this story, on one axis.
labels: Acres and megawatts are not one axis.
"Power is the one requirement we are shortest on."

slides.headline: It passed the Senate. Then it stopped.
slides.body: SB 250 would have required commission approved contracts so a data center's infrastructure and service costs are borne by the operator rather than shifted to other customers. It passed the Alaska Senate on May 16, 2026 and died in House Community and Regional Affairs.
labels: SB 2 . STATE AGENCY AI AND ELECTION DEEPFAKES
SB 250, SEN. LOKI TOBIN . SB 2, SEN. SHELLEY HUGHES

slides.headline: A pledge asks. A contract binds.
labels: BINDS NOBODY. VOLUNTARY AND NON BINDING.
BINDS EVERY UTILITY IN THE STATE.
BINDS ONE NAMED CUSTOMER TO NAMED TERMS.
SB 250 WOULD HAVE CREATED IT. NEVER BUILT.
The widest word on this page is the one that does not exist.

slides.headline: The other answer is to leave the grid entirely.
slides.body: Rep. Nick Begich of Alaska introduced the DATA Act on April 21, 2026. He says it lets manufacturers run on fully self contained grid of one power systems.
labels: SHARED RAIL . COSTS ARE ALLOCATED BY CONTRACT
OWN FOOTING . NO SHARED SYSTEM TO ALLOCATE
Two instruments, opposite mechanisms. One regulates the joint, one removes it.

slides.headline: A promise is not an instrument.
slides.body: Twenty three governors signed. One Alaska utility signed. Neither signature is a rule.
labels: Save this for the next time somebody promises your bill is safe.

aftercare: Post this draft on a Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday between 8 and 11am Alaska time, which is this audience's strongest window, and hold it rather than firing it into a Friday afternoon.
Paste the sources comment within 60 seconds of publishing, then work the golden hour and reply substantively to every comment in the first 60 to 90 minutes.

Deck specific warning, the only Alaska entity line is dated to the White House list read on July 26, 2026, so if a Railbelt utility signs after that date, concede it in the thread and repeat the read date rather than defending the claim.

Two live docket dates will come up from commenters, August 13 for the Houston City Council vote and August 19 for the DNR comment close, so have both at hand, and check saves and comments again at 48 hours.

copy_changes.now: CORDOVA DATA CENTER, 150 kW, ON HYDRO

copy_changes.why: House style sets these compounds open across the deck, and an open compound cannot be mistaken for a dash by any lint.

copy_changes.now: Rep. Nick Begich of Alaska introduced the DATA Act

The pixel critic caught the ISO date breaking across a line at its hyphen, which is a craft failure in a drafting-voiced deck and briefly reads as a truncated string. Dropping DUNLEAVY sets the date on one line; the governor is already named on slides 3 and 9.
